fact: The Bank of Mauritius states the National Payment Systems Act 2018 empowers it to regulate, oversee and supervise payment systems and to license payment service providers, with licensing regulations (National Payment Systems (Authorisation and Licensing) Regulations 2021) applying; the date is the document's publication month, July 2026, as it gives none for the Act's effect.
The Bank of Mauritius Guideline for Payment Aggregators, issued under section 17 of the National Payment Systems Act 2018, comes into effect on 31 August 2026.

The Guideline says non-bank bodies corporate that want to act as payment aggregators must obtain a payment service provider licence from the Bank of Mauritius under the National Payment Systems Act 2018 (section 9) and the 2021 licensing regulations, and existing non-bank aggregators must apply by 31 August 2026.

Section 17 of the AML/CFT/CPF (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2026 (Act No. 3 of 2026, assented 17 April 2026) amends the National Payment Systems Act (2018), adding rights of judicial review of Bank of Mauritius administrative penalties and actions against operators, participants and payment service providers, so that Act is in force and applied by the central bank.

The consolidated text of the National Payment Systems Act 2018 (Act 17 of 2018) lists amendments in force through Act 3 of 2026 (18 April 2026), and makes the Bank of Mauritius regulator of national payment systems, with power to issue binding directives and guidelines (s.4, s.17).

Section 9(1) of the National Payment Systems Act 2018 (Act 17 of 2018) provides that no person other than the central bank or a bank may act as a payment service provider without a licence from the Bank of Mauritius, and s.2 and s.45 cover electronic money and mobile payment systems; the consolidated text runs through amendments to April 2026.

The National Payment Systems Act 2018 (Act No. 17 of 2018) was passed by the National Assembly on 21 November 2018 and assented on 29 November 2018, making the Bank of Mauritius regulator of payment systems, payment service providers and electronic money; the text says commencement is by Proclamation, with no commencement date given in this document.

Section 9(1) of the National Payment Systems Act 2018 bars anyone other than the Bank of Mauritius or a bank from acting as a payment service provider without a Bank of Mauritius licence, and section 45 sets the further conditions for licensed issuers of electronic money (Schedule 1 item 9 lists e-money issuance as a payment service).
